text:
sanjay: Uploaded a draft runbook for AZ11 provisioning to /docs/runbooks/az11-bootstrap.md — wants review on known-issues + quick fixes. TL;DR: IPAM changes, GPU SKU mapping (A100/80GB primary, fallback to A10G), kernel/driver expectations, and cost guidance. https://git.internal/r/redwood/runbooks/pull/4523

infra-bot: runbook created and PR opened (#4523) by sanjay — CI checks pending :gear:

elaine: skimmed it. Couple quick nits: 1) call out required node image (ubuntu-22.04 + cuda 12.2 runtime). 2) explicit step to validate nvidia kernel module load on first boot (modprobe + dmesg).

devon: I'll add a short troubleshooting block for the "kubelet NotReady after device plugin crash" pattern we saw in eu-west. Steps: check device-plugin logs, restart ds, verify node labels.

zoe: GPU quota note: AZ11 has a lower A100 quota in the region right now. Recommend a fallback strategy in the runbook: (a) prefer A100 80GB; (b) if quota refused, try A10G or 1-2x 40GB variant. Also add per-instance hourly cost estimates so infra planning can choose reserved vs burst capacity.

tim: networking gotcha we hit before — host MTU=9000 but CNI defaults to 1500 which causes fragmentation for large RDMA-ish transfers. Add a check and the iperf command in the checklist: `sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 9000` on host and `iperf3 -s` / `iperf3 -c` between pods to verify.

samarth: driver / device-plugin quick checks I'm adding now:
```
# driver version
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader
# device plugin logs
kubectl -n kube-system logs daemonset/device-plugin -c nvidia-device-plugin
```
Also add `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | grep device-plugin` to confirm one-per-node.

elaine: Known issue to add: intermittent BMC watchdog reboots observed on a subset of G5 instances after a firmware rollout — manifests as nodes cycling through "NotReady -> Kubelet registration -> Ready" every ~10 minutes. Workaround: pin node firmware to previous build or set cloud provider health-check grace period to 5m until vendor patch.

devon: Also include a short section on device naming drift: sometimes the GPU bus ids change after kernel updates -> device-plugin may report different UUID ordering. We fixed by using the nvidia-container-runtime config that references UUIDs, and by adding a post-boot syspath verify step.

tim: networking rate/limits: cloud provider sometimes rate-limits allocation of secondary IPs on large subnets during bootstrap. Terraform may fail with 429s — add exponential backoff and `max_retries` on the provider resource (snippet):
```hcl
resource "provider_secondary_ips" "pods" {
  count = var.node_count
  max_retries = 8
  retry_sleep = "15s"
}
```
And a note: if you see bursts of 429, wait 10-15m then re-run the apply in smaller batches.

zoe: another known issue: CNI plugin occasionally leaks routes when nodes are terminated quickly -> results in pod-to-pod connectivity blips. Add an ip route cleanup step to the troubleshoot guide: `ip route flush table 100` (adjust table as needed).

samarth: checklist for quick post-bootstrap validation (short, copy/paste):
```
# basic cluster health
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl get cs
# confirm device plugin and drivers
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,uuid,driver_version --format=csv
kubectl -n kube-system logs daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin
# networking smoke
iperf3 -s &  # on a pod
iperf3 -c <pod-ip> -t 10
# check kube-proxy and CNI
kubectl -n kube-system get pods | grep -E "(kube-proxy|calico|cilium)"
```
I'll paste example successful outputs into the runbook so on-call has a quick compare.

infra-bot: scheduled smoke-test job `smoke/az11-bootstrap` to run in 20 minutes — results will post here.

zoe: cost note — for prod traffic profile we estimate baseline 120 pod-gpu hours per day. If committed 6-month reserved capacity, that's ~30% savings vs on-demand. Add the math table and a pointer to finance for confirmation.

devon: operational fallback: if control-plane latency to AZ11 >200ms, runbook should instruct to flip traffic to dedicated region (az7) and mark az11 as degraded in ops dashboard. Include the exact alert threshold rule.

sanjay: This is great — can someone drop the Terraform backoff PR and the device-plugin troubleshooting snippet into the runbook PR? I'll merge after CI and one more read.

samarth: done — added the snippets and a short troubleshooting flowchart. PR updated.

elaine: also added a "known issues" TL;DR at the top of the doc so on-call sees common flakes (BMC reboots, provider 429s for IPs, CNI MTU mismatch).

sanjay: I'll land the PR this afternoon after smoke test results. Thanks all :clap: If infra-bot posts failures, I'll reassign.

infra-bot: smoke-test `smoke/az11-bootstrap` started. Logs will follow in thread.
